  PUBLIC COMMENT ON  The following individuals spoke in support and advocated for
  MATTERS NOT ON THE  affordable housing efforts, including housing for the homeless,
  AGENDA  rent control, and additional tenant protections:

  Armando Herman, residence not stated
  Anthony Manousos, Greater Pasadena Affordable Housing
  Group (GPAHG)
  Bert Newton, GPAHG
  Debra A Johnson, Pasadena resident
  PJ Johnson, residence not stated

  Laura Hackett, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns with the
  tree removal and solar energy installation at Don Benito
  Elementary School adjacent to the playground areas.

  In response to public comment, Councilmember Gordo requested
  that staff follow up with Pasadena Unified School District
  regarding the proposed trees to be removed at Don Benito

  Council Minutes  2  12/09/20 19·
   Elementary School and other school sites; and the lack of public

0  notice of the tree removal.

  In response, City Manager Mermell stated that he would convey
  the concerns of the City Council and the public to PUSD's
  Superintendent.

  Vice Mayor Hampton requested that staff agendize for Public
  Safety Committee discussion, security and safety concerns at
  METRO rail stations. City Manager Mermell responded that he is
  working with Metro representatives to attend a future City Council
  meeting in the near future to discuss all the concerns raised at
  past Council meetings.

  Kea Vegan, Pasadena resident, requested assistance with a 60-
  day notice (Notice to Quit) she received regarding her rental
  agreement claim and the City's Tenant Protection Ordinance
  (TPO) as her rental management company is not abiding by the
  City's ordinance.

  Councilmember McAustin asked staff to provide additional TPO
  enforcement and suggested looking into the terms of company's
  business license regarding their ability to do business in the City.

0  Councilmember Gordo suggested the City commit additional
  resources to enforce the City's TPO regulations.

  Councilmember Kennedy requested that staff analyze the
  Housing Department to ensure that adequate resources exist to
  support TPO enforcement. In addition, he spoke on the need to
  adequately fund affordable housing in the City and determine if a
  funding stream can be developed for this much needed resource;
  with the item to be agendized at the appropriate City Council
  committee.

  In response to Councilmember McAustin's inquiry related to what
  is the City's recourse for landlords who do not abide by the City's
  TPO, Michele Beal Bagneris, City Attorney/City Prosecutor, stated
  that there are civil remedies, and depending on the circumstances
  possible complaints may result in the filing of a criminal case.

  In response to public comment, City Manager Mermell responded
  that he will discuss with staff and contact Ms. Vegan to address
  her concerns; and will agendize the approval of additional
  resources to the Housing Rights Center to assist tenants at the
  next City Council meeting.

  OFFICERS AND  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council

  David Reyes, Director of Planning and Community pevelopment,
  Arlene Granadosin-Jones, Planner, and Andre Sahakian, Senior
  Planner, presented a PowerPoint presentation, and jointly,
  responded to questions. Barbara Kautz, Attorney with Goldfarb &
  Lipman LLP, summarized housing State legislation that modifies
  local legislation and control; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Madison spoke on the need for staff to develop a
  comprehensive approach to a housing policy with a diverse

D  housing stock; and supported the City moving forward with the
  City's legislative agenda to continue to push for the resources the
  City needs.

  Councilmember Wilson expressed concerns with the state
  mandates that are not consistent with the key assumptions of the
  City's General and Specific Plans, and staff's plan to move
  forward updating those plans by spending a large sum of money
  under the changing dynamic of the State's legislation and what
  amounts to be a moving target.

  Councilmember McAustin expressed concerns with Accessory
  Dwelling Units (ADU's) parking requirements, which allows
  individuals to park their vehicles in random fashion. She
  expressed concerns with legislation related to super density
  bonuses, which allows a developer an 80% density bonus on a
  100% affordable project. She stated the need to find a way, by
  legal action or working with the state, to help educate the State
  legislature and make them understand that local control is
  necessary to manage development in the City; and research what
  action other municipalities are taking to keep local control over
  l_and use decisions; suggesting that if a developer proposed a
  project over the City's development caps, it should require a
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review.

  Council Minutes  13  12/09/2019
   Councilmember Gordo suggested that staff revisit the City's major
  transit routes and stops to ensure the City understands the precise
  impacts created by Assembly Bill 1763 on surrounding
  neighborhoods adjacent to such stops. He also stated that staff
  should review all the Specific Plans in context with all the changes
  in legislation, including the underline thresholds in order to assess
  any appropriate changes. Councilmember Gordo state that he
  believes that staff must be aggressive in the defense of the City's
  local control, and would like additional information on what
  thresholds are flexible related to the proposed state mandates,
  including thresholds specifically related to buffer zones. He asked
  staff to invite the City's state representatives to the City Council
  for an opportunity to question them on their legislative platforms
  and work with them to change the course of the state's mandates
  that are being pressed on the City. In addition, he spoke in favor
  of considering litigation against the state over the local control
  issue and requesting other cities to join with Pasadena.

  The Mayor spoke in opposition to staff reviewing transit stops as
  he doesn't see the City stripping transit or reducing thresholds in
  order to avoid triggering legislation; and expressed concerns with
  the City's ability to protect single-family neighborhoods. He spoke
  in favor of working and strategizing with state legislators on where
